HIVE — MAIN CHARACTER RIG (AUTO PREVIEW v6)

Rebuilt from the new true-side-profile parts sheet instead of the face-on catalog panel — this is the fix for the jumping-jack problem. Same knee/elbow follow-through walk cycle as v2, now driving near/far limb pairs instead of left/right (a true side view only shows one leg + one arm silhouette, duplicated for depth) so the swing actually reads as forward/back motion.

What this is: the 10 named parts from the new true-side-view sheet (one of each — no left/right this time), duplicated into a "near" and "far" copy for each limb (near drawn in front of the torso, far drawn behind it, same trick every 2D side-view game uses for depth), auto-stacked into a standing paperdoll with no manual placement. Known issue, not yet fixed: this generation's parts came out noticeably more elongated (especially thigh and forearm) than the first sheet's proportions, so the auto pose reads too slender/stretched — the character editor's per-part width/height controls are the place to bring that back to normal proportions, same as the rough joint overlap.

v4 knee/elbow fix: the earlier "delayed drag" knee motion was too subtle to read on limbs this long — it never looked like an actual bend. Replaced it with a stance/swing-gated fold: zero knee rotation through the whole stance half of the cycle (leg planted, straight, bearing weight) and a single pronounced fold peaking at mid-swing (foot lifted, clearing the ground) — matching where real knee flexion actually peaks, instead of a uniform pendulum with no distinction between "planted" and "recovering." Same gating on the elbows. Pelvis roll (hips tilt toward whichever leg is planted), opposite-phase torso counter-twist (contrapposto), arm-opposite-leg swing, and the body bob peaking at each leg's passing pose are all still in from v2/v3.
